nodes.label: Db Interface Contract (query/exec/withTransaction/close)
nodes.rationale: The shipped interface has four methods, not the two the plan's briefs describe; exec exists because multi-statement SQL needs the simple protocol, and withTransaction goes through sql.begin() because postgres-js is a pool where raw begin/commit can land on different connections.

nodes.label: Money Primitives (Paise/Cents branded bigint)
nodes.rationale: mulP goes through integer micros truncating toward zero and parseMinorUnits rejects sub-paise precision, so no rounding ever happens in floating point.

nodes.label: Planning Assumptions (PRD 15.2)
nodes.rationale: salaryStepUp is a separate key from sipStepUp on purpose (equal today, must not be re-merged) because take-home and SIP escalation are independent decisions.

nodes.label: Cash Ceiling Owner Rail (10%)
nodes.rationale: The PRD gave no cash number and the seeded 20% was invented; the owner set 10% on 2026-09-19 as an amendment, written byte-identically into PRD 3.3 and src/config/ips-v1.ts so ips-verbatim fails if they drift. CASH is classify()'s CASH class only, so EPF, bonds and liquid/debt funds do not count.

nodes.label: B3 Emergency Fund Excluded From the Cash Ceiling
nodes.rationale: Holding the emergency fund the IPS mandates is compliance, not idleness, and the 6L target is 10.7% of the 55.97L base so a funded B3 would trip the rail. Only the funded balance in bucket_flows is excused, never the target; bucket_flows is queried directly because buckets.ts re-exports the reporting-only FI metric and the firewall test refuses a risk function any path to it — including the identifier appearing in a comment.

nodes.label: The Rails Engine Reports, It Does Not Gate
nodes.rationale: checkRails is imported by digest.ts and never called; validateOrderGate checks staleness and FR-11/12 structure only; checkFreeze/setFreeze/recordFalsification are referenced only by their own tests; last_rail_change has three readers and no writer. The only live path is checkPortfolioRails feeding the digest breach list and /rails, so the Phase 2 ledger's 'rails enforced' must not be read as enforced on the order path.

nodes.label: checkPortfolioRails False TACTICAL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
nodes.rationale: It sums the whole EQUITY/ETF/MF book's market value against a per-month flow budget — a stock compared to a flow — so it fires permanently for any portfolio over 50k. The per-order version in checkRails is correct. Not yet fixed.

nodes.label: settings_rails Keys Carry Their Unit in the Name
nodes.rationale: _pct is a percent and _paise is money; the retired dotted cash.ceiling was a bare fraction. The /rails page pushed everything through a x100 Pct formatter and printed the new percent-valued rail as 1000.0%, so it now formats by key suffix.

nodes.label: Next.js web/ Bundling Contract
nodes.rationale: web/ was never typechecked and imported three symbols that did not exist. Nothing in src/ may read a file at module scope because webpack rewrites new URL(..., import.meta.url) into an inert asset handle and Vercel never ships the file; every page carries force-dynamic so next build opens no DB connection.

nodes.label: src/config/ips-v1.ts as a Template Literal
nodes.rationale: Converting the IPS from a .md read at module scope to a TS template literal deleted the domain-ips-shim and its NormalModuleReplacementPlugin — and exposed a bug the shim had masked: postgres-js returns a Date for timestamptz while PGlite returns a string, so any Promise<{...: string}> over a timestamp column is a lie the PGlite suite cannot catch.

nodes.label: Fidelity RSU Ingestion Flow
nodes.rationale: Proposals are priced with the SAME UNITS_SCALE/toUnitsMicros that rsu.ts exports, so the proposal's gross equals confirmVest's recomputed gross and net <= gross passes by construction. Grants are never auto-created (FR-02) and skipped entries are consumed so a stuck entry cannot silently block later confirmations.

nodes.label: Kite Retired — INDmoney Is the Only Portfolio Source
nodes.rationale: Kite worked on its first real run and that is how the bug surfaced: INDmoney already aggregates the same Zerodha account, so net worth jumped 26% with no money moving. Owner chose to drop Kite rather than build a precedence rule; the token also expired daily with no refresh token, making unattended sync impossible anyway.

nodes.label: loadPositions Reconciles Seed vs Live Only
nodes.rationale: Live-live rows are never merged — each source manages its own aggregation — which is correct while INDmoney is the sole live source but silently sums the moment a second live source covers the same account. The precondition now lives in the docstring so the next source cannot repeat it.

nodes.label: Never Feed JSON.stringify to a ::jsonb Placeholder
nodes.rationale: postgres-js stores a stringified object as a jsonb SCALAR STRING, so payload->>'...' reads NULL and the whole production audit trail was SQL-opaque; PGlite parses either form, which is why 417 green tests missed it. Fixed at all 8 write sites by passing the object.

nodes.label: PGlite vs postgres-js Driver Divergences
nodes.rationale: PGlite returns bigint columns as JS numbers and date columns as Date objects, and is a single connection so a query on the outer Db still lands inside an open transaction — which means transaction wrapping must be mutation-checked by removing withTransaction outright, not by moving a statement out of it.

nodes.label: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY Rotation
nodes.rationale: The old key was found in plaintext in this repo's own Claude Code transcripts; recovery was possible and deliberately declined in favour of rotation. A recover-key.yml workflow that echoed the secret into a run log was written and deleted unrun — it converts one lost secret into a permanent leak.

nodes.label: .env Values Must Be Unquoted
nodes.rationale: Node's --env-file strips quotes but a hand-rolled loader (web/next.config.ts) does not, so a quoted api_key produced api_key=%22...%22 and a live Kite InputException. A UTF-8 BOM in front of the first KEY= would make that key silently invisible.

nodes.label: INDmoney MCP networth_holdings Contract
nodes.rationale: The original mapper was written against an invented fixture and its three tests passed by feeding the invention back to itself. Real contract: asset_type is required, the reply is an envelope, invested_amount can be the string 'unknown', investment_code is polymorphic, the same instrument arrives once per broker/folio and MUST be aggregated, and a rate-limited call returns successfully with an error object — reading that as 'no holdings' would wipe the portfolio, so it is fatal.

nodes.label: Bond invested_amount Is Face Value, Not Cost
nodes.rationale: The API returns units x face, so the shipped mapper wrote face value straight into cost; aggregate() now returns avgCostPaise = null for every BOND row. total_pnl is computed against face too and understates true unrealised by 20,000.43, and the payload returns a stale pre-rebrand issuer name, so the single-issuer cap cannot be derived from it.

nodes.label: Loan Cascade — Owner-Verified Figures and Closures
nodes.rationale: Every loan comes from a real lender statement and reconciles arithmetically, so the PRD's stale 36.7L total loses. The plan's reference runCascade amortized sequentially and failed its own flat-outflow criterion by construction; the concurrent rewrite is correct. Closure dates are derived from closures, never written as literals — two earlier literal sets in this file were wrong.

nodes.label: Investable Surplus Curve
nodes.rationale: 82,124/month is derived, never hardcoded, and the ~6,124 gap against the PRD's 76,000 is an open owner true-up — not electricity, which the misc bucket already includes. The coverage guard keys off the outflow map's own range because closures is persisted nowhere and would silently no-op for a consumer reading a schedule back from Postgres.

nodes.label: RSU Vest Projection (cumulative tranche allocation)
nodes.rationale: Tranches are allocated cumulatively so 16 parts always sum back to the whole grant; rounding each independently (the plan's sketch) leaves a projection whose parts need not add to its whole. FR-03 is enforced in SQL by a unique (grant_id, vest_on) + conditional upsert, because the original read-then-write was check-then-act and a confirmVest landing in the window left an ACTUAL-labelled row carrying model numbers.

nodes.label: FI Corpus Band (income varies, SWR is a separate axis)
nodes.rationale: The shipped code took one income and varied only the SWR, so stretch came back BELOW the floor target and stretchRatio exceeded floorRatio for every input — the owner would have read 'better funded against the harder goal'. buckets.ts now re-exports the single model so the funded-status allowlist cannot be sidestepped through buckets.fundedRatio.

nodes.label: Signal Engine (section 6 quality gate + composite)
nodes.rationale: Two different 'no score' shapes on purpose: blocked by a stale input returns null (no score exists), a failed quality gate returns a row with qualityPassed false so the weekly report can say WHY a name was rejected. The gate fails closed on unknowns, mirroring FR-02. What it cannot see (EV/EBITDA, a name's own 5y P/E range, the G-sec yield) is declared rather than faked.

nodes.label: Allocation Engine (one net-worth basis, tax preference)
nodes.rationale: Two independent numbers describing one portfolio is how a caller gets silently wrong percentages, so rebalanceRec throws when positions disagree with netWorth. Tax awareness is one preference, not an engine: dilute with new money before selling, order trims losses-first with unknown cost basis last, and TAX_POLICY_NOTE states plainly what is NOT computed because we hold aggregated positions, not per-lot acquisition dates.

nodes.label: Sell / Exit Triggers (section 6.5) and the Falsification Grammar
nodes.rationale: recommendations.primary_rec carries a closed falsification grammar; a condition naming a datum we do not hold is untestable and returns null, because false and unknown are different answers. Only triggers 1-3 override the IPS 3.7 twelve-month hold; 4 and 5 surface with blockedByMinimumHold so the owner sees the engine wanted out and the IPS said wait. Data is cut at month END.

nodes.label: FR-11/FR-12 Recommendation Objects + Paper Mode
nodes.rationale: A1 falls back to the index route because buying the market is the honest expression of 'we want this exposure but have no edge on which name carries it'; A2 must carry a different intent and defaults to do-nothing priced as a real option. Every IPS citation is validated against the rendered clause index — a citation the owner cannot look up is worse than none. FR-12 caps LOG to suppressed_actions rather than dropping, and paper mode defaults TRUE when the rail is absent.

nodes.label: Weekly Deep Report + Narration (FR-51)
nodes.rationale: FR-31 covers yesterday's recommendations too: an open recommendation whose instrument is blocked today is withheld, not deleted, because you cannot act on what you cannot value. Narration receives finished engine output and nothing feeds back, so a missing narrative never costs the owner the report. Blank GSEC_YIELD_PCT means NOT CONFIGURED, never 0, because a 0% risk-free rate scores every name as cheap.

nodes.label: Scoring Harness (section 13 calibration)
nodes.rationale: The creation snapshot is immutable in SQL — UPDATE is allowed only on the eval columns — because blanket append-only made evals unwritable while dropping the trigger would let a bad week be re-based after the fact. An unscoreable call is recorded with its reason and never counted as a miss; below MIN_EVALS_FOR_CALIBRATION the table says 'insufficient data' rather than a percentage.

nodes.label: Screener Cohort Promotion (screen rows become instruments)
nodes.rationale: Identity is an inference, not a fact: NSE:<slug> is trusted only to be internally consistent with bhavcopy resolution, the name comes from the screen, and ISIN is deliberately left NULL for backfill:isin rather than invented. Degenerate /company/id/<n>/ rows resolving to slug 'ID' are refused because the LIKE fallback once substring-matched NSE:LIQUIDBEES.

nodes.label: SCREENER_COLUMNS Spec Was Written From Imagination
nodes.rationale: A real screen overlaps SCREENER_COLUMNS on P/E alone, so a real export parses to zero usable rows; Symbol, Industry, FCF 5Y and Red Flags have no native column while the quality gate reads two of them. Deliberately not patched by guessing a second mapping — it needs one real exported file plus an owner decision.

nodes.label: parseScreenPaste (signed-in CSV/TSV path)
nodes.rationale: The public page serves only 13 old columns; Profit Var 5Yrs %, Sales Var 5Yrs % and Free Cash Flow 5Yrs exist only in the signed-in author view, so the owner's export is the live test. Delimiter is auto-detected and repeated header rows reset the column map because screener repeats headers every ~15 rows on paginated exports.

nodes.label: NSE Bhavcopy Archive-First With Whole-Market Fallback
nodes.rationale: The archive host 404s every 2026 date while still serving 2019-2024, so equity prices had silently stopped landing in June. Archive stays primary because it is the only shape carrying an ISIN column; the fallback uses a NUMERIC month (the alphabetic-month name 404s there) and full-market rows are resolved through the NSE:<symbol> id instruments already carry. Both missing returns empty and is still reported honestly.

nodes.label: ISIN Backfill Is Fill-Only, Never Clobber
nodes.rationale: Only NSE:% ids with NULL/empty isin are filled from EQUITY_L.csv, never overwriting an owner-verified seeded value, and backfilling cannot create an instrument. Caveat: re-seeding overwrites backfilled values because seed.ts upserts isin = excluded.isin.

nodes.label: NSE Trading Calendar and isTradingDay
nodes.rationale: The weekend-only rule was wrong in both directions: it asked NSE for a file on ~15 holidays and would have skipped Sunday Muhurat trading when the exchange IS open. The asymmetry sets the bar for adding a date — a missing holiday costs one loud failed step, a wrong holiday silently starves every price-dependent engine, so when in doubt leave it out.

nodes.label: LLM Shortlists the Watchlist, Engine Owns Every Number
nodes.rationale: The division that keeps PRD 6.7 intact: the model proposes names and one sentence of reasoning while the engine decides everything carrying a number. Enforced in code, not trusted to the prompt — a pick must already exist in instruments, held names are excluded, and rows land as proposals awaiting sign-off.

nodes.label: One Model Family, Split by Capability (text vs vision)
nodes.rationale: The finance model is text-only and physically 400s on an image upload, so TEXT_MODEL is kept out of VISION_MODEL_CHAIN by test; vision reverted to the proven gemma leader after the vl trial. Tests assert wiring by DERIVING from the constants, never by restating a model id — the two that hard-coded a model id went red on the swap.

nodes.label: Four Artifacts Written From Imagination and Presented as Spec
nodes.rationale: The 40 watchlist names, SCREENER_COLUMNS, the 'shipped' screener staleness check and the 'shipped' bhavcopy downloader were all invented and recorded as delivered. Anything describing an EXTERNAL format or universe is a hypothesis until it has touched the real thing, and a ledger entry is a lead, never evidence — grep for the symbol.

nodes.label: The Starter Watchlist Has an LLM-Origination Problem
nodes.rationale: All 40 seeded rows are labelled source 'advisor' but were written by an LLM from training recall with no market data; the engine scores only what sits in that table, so the LLM originated the universe even though it never originates a score — in tension with PRD 6.7.

nodes.label: Owner True-Up Items
nodes.rationale: Open data questions that need real statements and must never be guessed: the RSU per-grant split (57.05L modelled vs PRD 53.25L), the missing milestones.raised_on column (the old hard-coded date was a fabricated figure shown to the owner as fact), the unsourced DEBT floor and CASH ceiling bands, basket decomposition, and the whole Indian equity book having no cost basis.

nodes.label: Deferred Minors Ledger
nodes.rationale: Tracked but not blocking, with an expected home rather than a hard schedule; genuinely cross-cutting items (unwrapped batch writes, the untested postgres-js path) stay for the fix wave while anything in a file you touch is fixed on the spot.

nodes.label: Seed/Live Double-Count and the Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Two live causes: id namespaces do not meet (only 3 of 47 rows carry an ISIN) and nothing ever retires manual-seed. Owner decision: the live source wins per (canonicalInstrumentId, account), but a holding a live source stops reporting falls back to the seed row rather than vanishing, which is safer against a partial API reply since staleness already flags the source.
